Correctness · pkg226 · #686

The default caustic was too bright

The default (non-poly) stochastic Newton SMS path — used by spectral_path_tracer and sms_caustic_path_tracer when sms_specular_poly is off — carried two coupled errors that over-brightened the glass-sphere caustic by roughly 1.5×.

Receiver-cosine double-count. evalSpectral already folds in the receiver cosine (lambertian.cpp returns albedo·cosθ/π), but runSMSAttempt multiplied the geometry factor G by cosX0 a second time — the receiver radiance carried cos² instead of cos. Biased seed-area pdf. The πr²/cosSeed reciprocal seed-sampling pdf (Zeltner 2020 biased variant) is meaningless once the Newton solve has converged to a deterministic vertex.

The fix drops both and adopts the exact MNEE chainGeometryTerm weight that the poly path (runSMSAttemptPoly, pkg127 / #685, same file) already uses for this sphere caster. Newton and poly now compute the same weight formula; the only remaining difference is Newton's single stochastic seed versus poly's exact enumeration. CPU-only; the function signature and all four call sites are unchanged.

Post-fix, Newton tracks poly closely: SSIM 0.987, per-channel mean ratio ~0.97 (measured caustic-region mean 71.97 vs 74.16 on these frames). The residual ~3–5% underestimate visible in the difference image is inherent to stochastic single-seed Newton at multi-solution foci — the poly path is exact and is the blessed reference (sms-refractive-glass-sphere already renders with sms_specular_poly=1, so the frozen baseline is untouched by this Newton-only fix).

On the image pair. These are not a before/after of the bug — both frames are post-fix. There is no rendered capture of the old ~1.5×-bright path; what is shown is the corrected Newton default beside the exact poly reference, demonstrating they now agree, with the difference image isolating the small residual bias that motivates keeping poly as the reference.
Correctness · pkg225-S6 · #684

GPU multiwavelength rendered every NEE-lit surface black

Reported as a curve/hair defect ("GPU spectral renders all GPRIM_CURVE hits black"). It was neither curve-specific nor shade-side — a plain lambertian sphere was equally black.

Root cause — module/blender_module.cpp. The GPU wavefront derived enableNEE from the integrator name:

bool enableNEE = (integratorName_ != "multiwavelength_path_tracer");

That hard-forced the GPU leg light-sampling-blind, while the CPU integrator takes enable_nee with default 1 (pkg195). In naive mode the wavefront accumulates emission only on bounce==0 || wasSpecular and the MIS w_B leg is itself NEE-gated, so a surface lit solely by an off-camera light received zero by construction. The GPU now reads the same param the CPU reads.

A second, independent defect in include/raytracer.h was found while wiring the spectral hair gates: Material::evalSpectralExt applied a wi·n ≤ 0 → 0 hemisphere gate, which deleted the Principled Hair TT/TRT lobes (they transmit through the fibre and carry most of its energy) and truncated subsurface / isotropic phase functions. All 19 evalSpectral implementations already self-gate correctly, so the wrapper's gate was redundant where correct and wrong where not.

Vacuous gates repaired. tests/baselines/pkg64-gpu-phase{2,3} Cornell baselines were pinned all-black (mean 0.0) — test_empty_hook_bit_equality had been certifying black-against-black for as long as this bug lived. Regenerated (mean 0.198) and guarded so an all-black frame can never be pinned again. Full suite: 2180 passed, 2 failed (both reproduce on a clean origin/main rebuild — pre-existing, attributed by baseline build). Built and HW-verified on the RTX 5070 Ti, .pyd arch-gate confirmed sm_120, 18/18 GPU tests. Independently reviewed; Opus-5-authored, double-checked by Opus 4.8.

Forward look · pkg227

Next: general specular-polynomials caustics

With the sphere caustic now correct on both the Newton and poly paths, the general solver was scoped this session and owner-approved (spec PR #687, open, merging). It generalizes pkg127's exact single-vertex sphere solver to accurate, fast, spectral caustics from arbitrary geometry.

Two tracks share the pkg127 spine: Track S extends the exact planar-sphere polynomial to a multi-bounce rainbow chain (refract → internal-reflect → refract — the raindrop rainbow, closed-form, low-degree, no tessellation); Track M ports Fan et al. 2024 (rational coordinate mapping + hidden-variable resultant) with interpolated shading normals for general triangle meshes. A decisive finding: the paper's per-tuple solver does not scale on its own — it needs an external Path-Cuts pruning structure Astroray lacks — so the phasing ships the cheap exact-sphere win and a single-caster smooth-mesh solver before the expensive pruning subsystem.

Implementation starts with Phase 2a — the analytic-sphere multi-bounce (raindrop rainbow, exact). Later phases: 2b flat single-caster mesh, 2b-smooth interpolated normals, 2c triangle-tuple pruning (deferred), 2d two-bounce mesh, 3 GPU mirror.
